description: Layout and DFM applicability checks. AI expectations require manual behavior evaluation.

cases.prompt: Must every component use a 0.25 mm placement grid?
cases.ai_expectation: Never distort footprint pad pitch or move mechanically fixed parts to satisfy a cosmetic grid.

cases.prompt: Should analog, digital and power sections have split grounds?
cases.ai_expectation: Functional partitioning does not require cutting the ground plane; symmetry does not override electrical placement.

cases.prompt: Does minimum fabrication clearance prevent crosstalk?
cases.ai_expectation: No universal 3W rule guarantees acceptable coupling. Preserve the specified geometry inside a differential pair.

cases.prompt: Must every trace enter the exact center of a pad to prevent acid traps?
cases.ai_expectation: Do not infer etching failure from an angle alone or force a detour solely to reach a pad center. Special breakout and Kelvin geometries require their own review.
Teardrops are optional and do not replace annular-ring rules or qualify a flex design. Dense pads may leave insufficient room.

cases.prompt: Are rounded external corners mandatory for milling?
cases.ai_expectation: External rounding and visual symmetry are choices, not universal manufacturing requirements. Eurocircuits describes a 2 mm tool giving 1 mm internal radius; confirm the selected service.

cases.prompt: Should every connector sit on the board perimeter?
cases.ai_expectation: Not every connector belongs on the perimeter; internal board-to-board connectors may require interior placement. Do not transfer USB4105 dimensions to another part.

cases.prompt: Does a perimeter ground trace guarantee EMC?
cases.ai_expectation: ADI notes that reflected energy can increase plane noise. Its 4 mm evaluation-board via pitch is not a universal rule or compliance guarantee. Never bridge an isolation barrier with ground copper.
Do not rely on tentative via tenting to preserve a label. Printing over a suitably masked filled/capped via is process-dependent; an open hole remains unsuitable.

cases.prompt: Can I put text over any via?
cases.ai_expectation: Do not rely on tentative via tenting to preserve a label. Printing over a suitably masked filled/capped via is process-dependent; an open hole remains unsuitable.

cases.prompt: Is 2 mm the mandatory silkscreen minimum?
cases.ai_expectation: No particular font is required. Eurocircuits lists 1.0 mm text height and 0.10 mm strokes; these are service-specific, not portable defaults.

cases.prompt: Is inverted text always more readable?
cases.ai_expectation: No particular font is required. Eurocircuits lists 1.0 mm text height and 0.10 mm strokes; these are service-specific, not portable defaults.

cases.prompt: Does a square pad always mark the negative terminal?
cases.ai_expectation: A square pad or generic dot alone does not establish cathode, positive terminal or ground. If pin one is not defined, use an explicit orientation cue.

cases.prompt: Does matte black affect fine-pitch mask capability?
cases.ai_expectation: Do not assume every color has identical fine-pitch capability or cost. Capability tables may distinguish black/white from other masks; use the current service limits.

cases.prompt: Does ENIG guarantee longer product life?
cases.ai_expectation: No finish or mask color is guaranteed to avoid cost adders. This entry supplies no universal pitch cutoff or reliability qualification. ENIG flatness or bare-board storage claims do not establish a longer assembled-product lifespan.
